title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 597–600 of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'): Grothendieck studies a group S_0Γ^!_{ρ,σ} of triples (u,a,b), where u lies in a group Z^!_{ρ,σ} = M^![0] and a ∈ N*_ρ, b ∈ N*_σ. Here ρ and σ are the standard elements of order 3 and 2, N*_ρ and N*_σ are their (extended) normalizers, and L_ρ, L_σ are their intersections with the profinite group 𝔊. Π̂_0 is a profinite normal subgroup and Π̂ = Π̂_0 × {±1}. The characters ε_2 and ε_3 take values in μ = {±1}. This is the 'loop equation' setting of the Teichmüller tower / Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory that continues La Longue Marche. The previous page built a set-theoretic section A : Z^! → S_0Γ^!, u ↦ (u, ε_3(τ')α^{-1}u, β^{-1}u). It showed that A is multiplicative over the two index-≤2 subgroups Z'^! = {ε_3(u)=1} and Z''^! = {ε_2(u)=ε_3(u)}, but not over all of Z^!.

Remark (61). Within the preimage S_0Γ'^! of Z'^!, the elements lying in the image of the section are characterised by u ≡ b ≡ a mod Π̂_0, together with ε_3(u)=1. This makes the subgroup property obvious, since the congruence conditions are stable under products. Grothendieck notes he found no equally 'pretty' congruence description for the image of the section over Z''^! (where ε_2ε_3 = 1).

Proposition (62). Remedy: weaken the congruence on a so that it holds modulo the larger group Π̂, with a twist by a sign. Define S_0^πΓ^! = {(u,a,b) ∈ Z×N*_ρ×N*_σ (over M[0]) : u ≡ b mod Π̂_0, u ≡ ε_3(·)a mod Π̂}. Then:
(a) S_0^πΓ^! is a subgroup. The next page proves this: the obstruction (56) [σ,u'] = ε'_3 now only needs to hold in 𝔊/Π̂, where the ε's become trivial because Π̂/Π̂_0 is central of order 2.
(b) The projection (u,a,b) ↦ u onto Z^! = M^![0] is surjective, because S_0^πΓ^! contains A(Z^!). Its kernel is {(1,ε,1) : ε ∈ μ}, where μ = N'_ρ ∩ Π̂ = L_ρ ∩ Π̂ ≅ {±1}. This uses (57): L_ρ∩Π̂ = L_σ∩Π̂ = μ and L_ρ∩Π̂_0 = L_σ∩Π̂_0 = 1.

Net result: the failure of the section to be multiplicative is absorbed into a central extension 1 → μ → S_0^πΓ^! → Z^! → 1. Over Z'^! and Z''^! this extension splits via A. In modern terms it is the familiar sign (±1) ambiguity in lifting automorphism data from the PSL_2 / B_3-level to the profinite fundamental group level, here handled through normalizers of the torsion elements ρ and σ.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. Kernel check: u=1 forces b ≡ 1 mod Π̂_0 with b ∈ N*_σ ∩ Π̂_0 = 1. It also forces a ∈ N*_ρ ∩ Π̂ = μ. This is consistent with (b) and (57).
The twisting sign in (62) is written ε_3(σ) (or possibly ε_3(u)); the previous page uses ε_3(τ'). The exact argument is ambiguous in the manuscript.
The remark leaves open a congruence characterisation of the section over Z''^!, as Grothendieck explicitly says; this is a small gap, not an error.

ideas.what: Set-theoretic section A of S_0Γ^! → Z^! that is multiplicative exactly over two index-2 subgroups, characterised by congruences mod Π̂_0
ideas.modern_name: partial splitting of a group extension; congruence description of a section
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard group theory; specific setting is Grothendieck's Teichmüller-tower/GT program
ideas.where_published: Unpublished continuation of La Longue Marche (cote 140-3)

ideas.what: Enlarging the congruence modulus from Π̂_0 to Π̂ = Π̂_0×{±1} to obtain a subgroup that maps onto Z^! with kernel μ={±1}
ideas.modern_name: central extension by μ_2 of a group of 'loop-equation' automorphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: analogous ±1 phenomena appear in Drinfeld/Ihara/Lochak–Schneps work on GT and in mapping-class/braid lifting
ideas.where_published: unsure; not in Esquisse or La Longue Marche as published excerpts to my knowledge

missed.claim: Grothendieck finds a clean congruence characterisation (u≡b≡a mod Π̂_0) of the image of the section over the subgroup ε_3=1. He states he could not find an analogous nice expression over the subgroup ε_2ε_3=1.
missed.quote: Je n'ai pas trouvé de jolie expression analogue pour l'appartenance d'un élément de S_0Γ''^!
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is minor and technical. It would only matter to someone reconstructing his loop-equation approach to GT-type groups in detail.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a technical working step in the unpublished GT/loop-equation notes: resolving a non-multiplicative section via a ±1 central extension. It is coherent and correct, but the phenomenon is routine and does not appear to contain an unknown result of broad significance.
transcription_corrections: 'qui appartiennent [?] [?] à la solution analogue aux constructions [?]' likely reads 'qui appartiennent à la section ensembliste construite (provenant de la prop. p. 598) sont caractérisés par la relation'.
'la relation correspondante' at the end of the remark likely reads 'la section correspondante'.
'Z^!_{ρ,σ}=M'[σ]' should read 'Z^!_{ρ,σ} = M^![0]'; likewise '$M[\sigma]$ [?]' under (62) is 'M[0]'.
In (62) the ambient set is Z_{ρ,σ}×N*_ρ×N*_σ written above a crossed-out symbol; the condition is 'u ≡ b (Π̂_0), u ≡ ε_3(σ) a mod Π̂ = Π̂_0×{±1}'.
'x-groupe' / 'sous-groupe' in the remark: 'qui rend évident que c'est un sous-groupe'.
Page number at top is 599 (Grothendieck's numbering); 590 is the archive scan number.
